translation:
If he had gone abroad, he would have to return to his own native land once his visa expired. But whoever dwells permanently in his own native land, no one can remove him from there. That is why Jivanji Maharaj has gone only to his own eternal abode (Swadham). Moreover, in that abode there is an assembly of great saints such as Sadguru Kabir, and so he asked the messengers who came to fetch him, again and again, whether Kabirji was there — for Sadguru Jivanji Maharaj is not separate from Kabirji, but is himself a part (limb) of Sadguru Kabirji.

Jivanji Maharaj appeared on this earth, by the command of the Supreme Being Kabirji and others, for the welfare of eligible souls. Twice, Jivanji Maharaj postponed death for the sake of the welfare of his devotees. When, in this way, the appointed time promised in a dream came due, the conversation he had with the messengers who came to fetch him was overheard by Panabai, the wife of his son Shyamdas.

Swadham (The Divine Abode)

_ham aaye un deshthi | phir jaano un desh ||_
_eh jugat banai jivana | sab santanke updesh ||_
(I have come from that other Land; know that I go back to that Land. This arrangement, O Jivan[a], is what all the saints teach.)

The individual soul separates (becomes parted) from the Supreme Brahma and comes into this world. Here it experiences pleasure and pain, and then, according to its karma, passes through the 8,400,000 species of life. Or else, according to its karma, it returns to the place it came from and reaches once again the presence of the Supreme Brahma. Sadguru Shri Jivanji Maharaj has shown the Uda Bhakt Ramkabir tradition the vision of this path, and has given the call to walk this simple path. Jivanji Maharaj has given the infinite presence of the Supreme Brahma the name "Undesh" (the Other Land). In this way, for all devotees departing this world, Jivanji Maharaj has shown the vision of this unique and wondrous divine play (leela) of the Supreme Brahma.

On the 8th day of the dark fortnight of Shravan in Vikram Samvat 1737, all the Uda Bhakt exclusive Vaishnavas gathered together in Puniyad. Jivanji Maharaj had invited everyone to come here. Welcoming that invitation, everyone gathered together, and a festival of Hari-kirtan (devotional singing) took place. Describing this occasion in beautiful poetic form, Nana Parekh writes:

_"Ramkabir satya chhe shri Dham Puniyad sakal santno nivas, tahaan Vaishnav Jivandasji birajey chhe, Hari kirtan maha mangal thay chhe, Vaishnav aavi malya chhe, je koi maha param sukh upaje chhe sneh din din adhik vadhe chhe, vrahe vairag vishvas aave chhe. Tamo krupanath chho, aatmane kahadva (uddhar karva) aavya chho."_
(Ramkabir is the truth; the holy abode Puniyad is the dwelling of all the saints. There Vaishnav Jivandasji resides. The great, auspicious Hari-kirtan takes place; the Vaishnavs have come and gathered; wherever this happens, a great supreme joy arises; love grows greater day by day; dispassion (vairagya) and faith come to flourish. You are the Lord of Mercy (Krupanath); you have come to draw out — to redeem — souls.)

_Sakhi:_
_Kabir kede pragate, jagma Jivandas |_
_Dhaja bandhi dharma dadhaviyo, jam kinkar paame traas ||1||_
(1. In Kabir's lineage, Jivandas has appeared in the world; having raised the flag, he has made dharma firm — the servants of Yama, seeing this, are struck with terror.)

_Vaishnavji's doha:_
_Kaanto haath Kabir ke, tahaan sakal dharma toliyo |_
_Jap tap tirath daan, ta mule mitho choliyo ||2||_
(2. In Kabir's hand is the balance-scale on which all dharma is weighed; japa (recitation), tapa (austerity), pilgrimage, and charity — set against its true worth, are no more than a sweet cholio, a chickpea.)

That dharma is primordial and eternal (sanatan); one may search the three worlds and the twenty-one universes, but no other dharma comes to equal it on the scale. All the saints were sitting together, and discourse and kirtan were going on. When one watch of the last part of the night remained, two Vaishnavs arrived and gave darshan to Vaishnav Jivandasji; no one else could see them — others could hear the conversation but could not see the visitors. One of them was a form of great beauty, holding a red staff in hand, fair of body, in the fullness of youth, without beard or moustache. That Vaishnav spoke to Vaishnav Jivandasji: "I have come to fetch you. There, Kabirji is present, and Rankaji, Namdevji, Seniji, Dhanaji, Pipaji, and Rohidasji are also there."

Vaishnav Jivandasji asked further, "Is Kabirji there?" The Vaishnav replied, "Yes, Kabirji is there." Vaishnav Jivandasji was filled with great joy.

Jivandasji said to those Vaishnavs, "Here, the Vaishnav children have great hope in me; I will come after six months." Those Vaishnavs said to Vaishnav Jivandasji, "Without you, things there are not proceeding well; we are waiting eagerly." Vaishnav Jivandasji said, "Give my greetings to the Vaishnavs, and say Ramkabir to them." After that, those Vaishnavs departed. The Vaishnavs present here, who had heard the conversation, asked, "O Maharaj! With whom did you converse? No one appeared to our eyes."

Vaishnav Jivandasji said: "Some Vaishnavs had come to fetch me. They pleaded a great deal; I have given a promise of six months." When twenty days remained of that promise, he summoned his own Vaishnavs; everyone came and sat together, and unbroken Hari-kirtan went on continuously, without interruption.

Vaishnav Jivandasji said: "Prepare the raw provisions; make khaja, jalebi, and kari-ladu." He appointed some of his own Vaishnavs for daily service. The day of Janmashtami arrived, and everyone came and sat together. Vaishnav Jivandasji spoke:

_Sakhi:_
_"Sadguru sandesa moklya, kyaan bacha sab aav |_
_Naam chintamani Jivana, je bhave so paav ||3||_
_Baal buddhu Jivana, Ram bhaktiki aash |_
_Shoorveer bhaagi chale, daante pakadi dhaash ||4||_
(3. The Sadguru has sent his message: "Come, all my children, wherever you are." The Name is the wish-fulfilling gem, O Jivan[a] — whoever holds it dear attains it.
4. Child and elder alike, O Jivan[a], hold the hope of devotion to Ram; the brave hero presses forward, gripping his resolve firmly, as if held between the teeth.)

"Brothers, if anyone tries to mislead you, do not be misled. The true Lord is the enchanting flute-player [Krishna]; if others — Brahma, the Vedas, and so on — are followed instead, they lead the soul away from the Supreme Brahma." For five days the festival of divine play continued, and all the Vaishnavs came. Four Vaishnavs stayed to render service; their names were: (1) Vaishnav Laldasji (2) Vaishnav Gopaldasji (3) Vaishnav Nadiyada Haridasji (4) Vaishnav Rupa Bhagat.

Here all the devotees came and gathered together. It was understood that this was the last occasion, and everyone wished for a final darshan of Jivanji Maharaj. At this time he called Shyamdasji near him, explained matters to him in detail, inquired about all the arrangements, and said: "Take this body to the garden at Shahpura and perform the cremation rites there. At Shahpura is holy ground, the land of the saints — make a [tulsi] plot there." Then Shyamdasji said:

_Tahaan Ayodhya jahaan Raghupati | Kaahanah tahaan Gokul gaam |_
_Sampuri tahaan Jivana | Jahaan sant sangat Harinaam ||_
(There is Ayodhya, wherever Raghupati [Ram] dwells; there is the village of Gokul, wherever Kanha [Krishna] is. Every place, O Jivan[a], is [as holy as] Sampuri, wherever there is the company of saints and the Name of Hari.)

Wherever Ram dwells, that is Ayodhya; wherever Krishna is, that is the village of Gokul. And wherever, in the company of saints, the Name of Hari is taken, those places are verily equal to the seven holy cities (Saptapuri).

Hearing this sakhi, Jivanji Maharaj was filled with great joy and began to say: "Before coming here, I lived in the presence of Sant Gopaldas; so, knowing this to be the wish of the Merciful Lord, and from the feeling that I would remain always in his presence, I have been insisting on Shahpura. But now, take me to the garden in Puniyad, perform the cremation rites there, and make a tulsi plot there."

Giving this instruction, he said, "I entrust the service to Kahandasji," and placed his own neck-mala upon Kahandasji. But the devotees said that this ought to remain in your own household; so Jivanji Maharaj instead wrapped the mala around Kahandasji's thumb, applied tilak to his thumb, and then, holding Kahandasji's hand, had him apply tilak to Shyamdasji — thereby appointing Shyamdasji as his successor. He then asked for water to be brought so he could bathe. He took his seat beneath the lemon tree behind the house and bathed with the water. Then the sisters Jetibai, Malibai, Baijibai, and Panabai, who had brought sukhadi as prasad, offered it to the Lord, and that prasad was distributed among all the Vaishnavs. At midnight, from Thuvavi, Lalbai came along with Rambai and Tulsidas and others; Vaishnavs came from Bhilapur; and from Shahpura, Mohandas brought kamod-rice prasad, which he partook of, and those present also shared and partook of it.

Finally, he gave his last teaching to all the Vaishnavs, urging them to remain vigilant. And, saying "Ramkabir" to Kandas and to Vaishnav Haridas who had come from Arithha, Jivanji Maharaj departed toward his own eternal abode. Haridas bowed at the feet of Jivanji Maharaj and said "Ramkabir."

Thus Jivandasji departed for Swadham at midnight on the 8th of the dark fortnight of Shravan — Janmashtami day — in Vikram Samvat 1730.
